title: NVDEC GPU VIDEO DECODE OPTIMIZATION & TIMESTAMP FORENSIC VALIDATION
summary: NVDEC hardware decoding works on GTX 1660 Ti. Timestamp/DTS errors originate upstream (Moblin/RTMP/MediaMTX), not from NVDEC. Software vs NVDEC A/B test shows identical DTS patterns. Stream copy test confirms timestamp issues exist before decoding. Audio stream is primary source of DTS regressions. Two-camera simultaneous NVDEC decode works. NVDEC fails safely on invalid device.

cam1.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -c:v h264_cuvid -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam1" -t 60 -map 0:v:0 -an -f null NUL

cam2.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -c:v h264_cuvid -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam2" -t 60 -map 0:v:0 -an -f null NUL

cam1.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam1" -t 60 -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy -f null NUL
cam1.key_finding: Timestamp regressions exist at packet level BEFORE any decoding. Confirms upstream origin.

cam2.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam2" -t 60 -map 0:v:0 -an -c:v copy -f null NUL
cam2.key_finding: CAM2 video stream copy shows clean timestamps. CAM1 shows severe upstream timestamp issues.

cam1_video_only.dts_warnings_stream_0_video: Present but moderate (see test_1 and test_2)

cam1_audio_video.dts_warnings_stream_1_audio: SEVERE: Massive DTS regressions on audio stream (1690422>=1652173, 2614688>=2613117...)
cam1_audio_video.key_finding: Audio stream (AAC) is the PRIMARY source of DTS non-monotonic warnings. Video DTS warnings are minor in comparison.

cam2_audio_video.key_finding: CAM2 audio+video test shows clean output. CAM2 has fewer timestamp issues than CAM1.

test_5_two_camera_simultaneous_nvdec.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -c:v h264_cuvid -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam1" -rtsp_transport tcp -c:v h264_cuvid -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam2" -t 30 -map 0:v:0 -map 1:v:0 -an -f null NUL
test_5_two_camera_simultaneous_nvdec.gpu_vram_bounded: Expected bounded (single GPU, two decoder contexts)

test_8_failure_fallback.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel warning -rtsp_transport tcp -c:v h264_cuvid -gpu 999 -i "rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/live/cam1" -t 10 -map 0:v:0 -an -f null NUL
test_8_failure_fallback.result: FAILURE - Clean error, no infinite retry
test_8_failure_fallback.error_message: cu->cuDeviceGet(&hwctx->internal->cuda_device, device_idx) failed -> CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE: invalid device ordinal
test_8_failure_fallback.decoder_error: Error while opening decoder: Generic error in an external library
test_8_failure_fallback.fallback_behavior: NOT_IMPLEMENTED_IN_APPLICATION - FFmpeg fails cleanly; application would need to implement fallback to software decode

nvdec_verification.decoder_engine_telemetry: NOT_VERIFIED - pynvml reports aggregate GPU utilization, not decoder-engine-specific utilization

application_pipeline_analysis.current_architecture: RTSP -> OpenCV VideoCapture (software decode) -> numpy CPU frames -> V2 ingestion -> AI pipeline
application_pipeline_analysis.decoder: OpenCV default (software H.264 via FFmpeg backend)
application_pipeline_analysis.audio_handling: OpenCV VideoCapture reads both video and audio streams; audio frames are discarded
application_pipeline_analysis.frame_contract: CanonicalFrame with numpy uint8 CPU memory (BGR pixel format)
application_pipeline_analysis.timestamp_handling: Wall-clock receive time used for live streams; ReplayClock for deterministic timestamps
application_pipeline_analysis.nvdec_integration_feasibility: Would require replacing VideoFrameIterator with custom FFmpeg/NVDEC pipeline. Current contract requires CPU numpy frames, so GPU->CPU transfer needed. Not zero-copy.

root_cause_classification.timestamp_dts_errors_origin: UPSTREAM - Moblin RTMP publisher timestamp generation and/or MediaMTX RTSP timestamp handling
evidence: Stream copy (no decode) shows identical/severe DTS regressions on CAM1
Software decode and NVDEC decode show similar DTS warning patterns
Audio stream is primary source of DTS warnings (stream 1)
CAM2 video stream copy shows clean timestamps - camera-specific upstream difference
No H.264 decode errors (missing reference picture, bad cseq, bytestream) observed during controlled tests

cam1_nvdec_vs_software.pattern_similarity: HIGH - both show clustered non-monotonic DTS at similar intervals
cam1_nvdec_vs_software.conclusion: Decoder choice does not materially affect DTS warning pattern

cam2_nvdec_vs_software.conclusion: Software decoder may expose more timestamp irregularities; NVDEC slightly cleaner

stream_copy_vs_decode.cam1_stream_copy: SEVERE DTS jumps (millions of timestamp units)
stream_copy_vs_decode.cam1_nvdec: Moderate DTS warnings (hundreds of timestamp units)
stream_copy_vs_decode.cam1_software: Moderate DTS warnings (hundreds of timestamp units)
stream_copy_vs_decode.conclusion: Decoder (both NVDEC and software) partially masks upstream timestamp issues; stream copy exposes raw packet timestamps

limitations: Decoder-engine-specific GPU utilization not available via pynvml (only aggregate GPU %)
CAM1 and CAM2 show different upstream timestamp quality - not identical sources
Audio stream DTS issues dominate the warning output when audio is enabled
Application pipeline currently uses OpenCV VideoCapture (software decode); NVDEC integration would require new FFmpeg pipeline
Zero-copy GPU->GPU path not feasible with current CanonicalFrame contract (requires CPU numpy)
60-second test duration; longer soak may reveal additional behaviors
GTX 1660 Ti NVDEC supports up to 4K H.264 - verified working at 3840x2160@30fps
Application-level NVDEC fallback not implemented - would need to be added if NVDEC integration proceeds
readiness_for_phase_36r: NOT READY FOR PHASE 36-R FINAL SOAK - Timestamp/DTS issues are upstream and not resolved. Phase 36B forensic investigation complete. Recommend addressing upstream timestamp generation (Moblin/MediaMTX) before long-duration soak.
